disposition_reason: Table 1 prints mean, SD, minimum and maximum lead, cadmium and arsenic in 24 raw milk samples from 12 cows on one farm next to a mineral concentrator and dump in the Mantaro Valley, Peru.

study.design: Single-farm case study of soil, pasture and raw milk with dietary risk assessment
study.origin: El Tambo district, Huancayo province, Junín, Peru (3214 m a.s.l.)
study.method: Dry ashing at 450 °C then HNO3; flame AAS (AOAC 973.35) for Pb, Cd and As
study.lod_text: Milk LOD Pb 0.03, Cd 0.03, As 0.028 µg/L; forage 2.40, 0.40, 0.03 µg/kg; soil 0.1, 0.01, 0.02 mg/kg
study.qa: Precision checked with standard solutions (Pb 155, Cd 150, As 50 mg/kg; measured 148, 152, 49.6); no milk CRM reported

findings.group: representative dairy farm, El Tambo, Huancayo, Junín (beside a mineral concentrator and former municipal dump)
findings.notes: 24 samples from 12 cows (April and May 2022). Flame AAS; stated milk LOD 0.03 µg/L. Table 1 MPL used by the authors for milk: Pb 0.02, Cd 0.003, As 0.014 mg/kg.

regulatory_or_exposure.what: Maximum permissible limits for milk used by the authors
regulatory_or_exposure.value: Pb 0.02, Cd 0.0026, As 0.014 mg/kg (Table 1 prints Cd 0.003)

regulatory_or_exposure.what: Hazard index above 1 for children under 7, 9 and 11 years at low, medium and high milk intake; arsenic target hazard quotient above 1

unresolved: Arsenic by flame AAS at 193.7 nm with a stated milk LOD of 0.028 µg/L is far below what flame AAS normally achieves; the LOD values may be mislabelled.
Soil and pasture values (Table 1) are not food findings: soil Pb 652.35, Cd 7.09, As 6.29 mg/kg; pasture Pb 23.17, Cd 0.250, As 0.063 mg/kg.
Whether raw milk is reported on fresh weight is implied (50 g homogenized milk ashed) but not stated.
